graphify/extractors/vbnet.py.behavior: Preserve namespace qualification on module/type calls, search the caller namespace and parents before global names, support an explicit Global qualifier, and leave ambiguous short names unresolved. The 0.9.73 first-short-name lookup could bind Beta.Helpers.Log to Alpha.Helpers.Log.
graphify/extractors/vbnet.py.oracle_adaptation: Three exact-context hunks in vbnet.py add namespace-aware owner lookup and a set of possible owners per short name. check_vbnet.py uses this adapted reference for the original suite, generated files and complete corpora; twelve new namespace cases supplement the existing oracle. The pinned archive is unchanged.

graphify/extract.py.behavior: Preserve Astro script bodies for quoted or unquoted JavaScript types and empty types. Read complete attributes and use only the first actual type attribute, so data-type and text inside another attribute cannot suppress executable code. Non-JavaScript types remain masked with line locations preserved.
graphify/extract.py.oracle_adaptation: Two exact-context hunks against Graphify 0.9.73 extract.py replace the backtracking negative lookahead with complete attribute parsing. check_extract.py applies extractor adaptations before rebinding the facade, compares explicit script-type cases, and records this deviation; the pinned archive is unchanged.

graphify/extract.py.behavior: EJS templates (Graphify 0.9.88, #3811) read inline <script> types with the same reviewed attribute parser as Astro and Svelte, so a quoted JavaScript type (type="module", type="text/javascript") keeps its body instead of being masked by the backtracking negative lookahead upstream shares between the three maskers.
graphify/extract.py.oracle_adaptation: One exact-context hunk against Graphify 0.9.88 extract.py makes _ejs_mask_non_script call _astro_script_is_javascript (added by the Astro hunk) instead of _NON_JS_SCRIPT_TYPE_RE; the pinned archive is unchanged.

graphify/cache.py.behavior: Validate portable source paths after interpreting the root marker; preserve walked-path isolation.
graphify/cache.py.oracle_adaptation: The pinned semantic identity helper strips only the literal $graphify-root$/ prefix before its existing path check; every other helper remains unchanged.

graphify/cache.py.behavior: Infer the walked directory root from the input file parent, preserving a final file symlink as its own source. Restore marked paths before ordinary relative paths, using the same walked root for both. A shared AST cache may move across canonical or symlinked checkouts without stale source paths or identifiers. Native schema 7 invalidates older affected records; the Linux-discovered relative-path restoration fix is compatible with schema 7 records.
graphify/cache.py.native_regression: cache_paths::directory_alias_tests::canonical_root_and_walked_files_restore_together_in_another_checkout; extract::tests::relocated_cache_preserves_walked_roots_and_file_symlinks (16 source/target pairs starting from a physical temporary directory so macOS /var aliases cannot mask relative-path entries); incremental::tests::missing_import_placeholders_follow_their_originating_files
graphify/cache.py.oracle_adaptation: Exact-context additions independently infer the walked directory prefix only when its full root-relative suffix agrees, restore marked values first, then anchor ordinary relative source fields under that same prefix. check_cache.py covers a fresh symlinked-root cache reused under a second checkout. Whole-extraction reference imports include the reviewed cache adaptation. Pinned source files remain unchanged.

graphify/cli.py.behavior: Invalidate rejected semantic cache entries in the current file/prompt/mode so ordinary retries can recover.
graphify/cli.py.native_regression: check_native_workflows.py: native semantic rejection followed by ordinary retry

graphify/cluster.py.behavior: The oversized-community and low-cohesion re-splits run the second Leiden pass at the caller's `resolution` instead of _partition's default 1.0, so `--resolution 0.5`/`2.0` is no longer undone by the follow-up passes; output is unchanged at resolution 1.0. The Rust `split_community` keeps the Python default signature (1.0) and `split_community_at` carries the explicit resolution.
graphify/cluster.py.oracle_adaptation: Four exact-context hunks to the pinned cluster.py: both `_split_community(G, nodes)` call sites pass `resolution`, the function gains `resolution: float = 1.0`, and it forwards `resolution=resolution` to `_partition`.

graphify/extractors/apex.py.behavior: Class/interface heritage clauses and method return types accept namespace-qualified and generic types; heritage names split on top-level commas, drop generic arguments and keep the tail segment (supersedes PR 3276).
graphify/extractors/apex.py.oracle_adaptation: The PR's _TYPE pattern, heritage_names helper, three regex edits and three heritage-loop rewrites are applied as five exact-context hunks to the pinned apex.py.

graphify/extractors/commonlisp.py.behavior: `define-condition` dispatches through the defclass handler (ahead of the data-definer fallback), so `(define-condition my-error (app-error) ...)` emits `inherits` edges to each superclass (stubbing unknown ones like `error`) instead of a plain data node with no hierarchy. Only the one-line dispatch change is adopted; the PR's separable `specializes`/ensure_class_ref changes are not.
graphify/extractors/commonlisp.py.oracle_adaptation: One exact-context hunk in _process_form of the pinned commonlisp.py: `if first_lower in ("defclass", "define-condition"):`.

graphify/extractors/markdown.py.behavior: The wikilink pattern captures the page (possibly empty) and the #heading fragment separately. A same-page anchor ([[#Setup]], or [[notes#Setup]] resolving to the current file) is deferred and, once the whole page is walked, emits heading --references--> heading (page --references--> heading above the first heading) when that heading exists and is not the source; each (source, heading) pair is emitted once, `[[]]` emits nothing, and [[Other#Sec]] still references the other page.
graphify/extractors/markdown.py.oracle_adaptation: Four exact-context hunks to the pinned markdown.py: the combined wikilink regex, an is_same_page helper plus pending_anchors list, the wikilink loop body, and the post-walk anchor edge emission before the return.

graphify/extractors/markdown.py.behavior: A table-escaped alias pipe (`[[notes/Target\|Alias]]`) is not part of the wikilink page: the page group is lazy and an optional backslash precedes the alias pipe, so the target resolves exactly like the unescaped `[[notes/Target|Alias]]`.
graphify/extractors/markdown.py.oracle_adaptation: Merged upstream in 0.9.72 with its own lazy page and escaped-pipe pattern; the combined _MD_WIKILINK_RE hunk shared with PR #3450 now replaces the 0.9.72 line, keeping the heading capture #3450 needs.

graphify/extractors/markdown.py.behavior: Prune ignored directories before descending and exclude ignored files from the vault-wide basename index (merged upstream in 0.9.71 as 57a263ce for issue #3822). Native additionally applies the rules under the canonical root while keeping walked link paths: upstream 0.9.71 passes walked paths under a symlinked root (macOS /var -> /private/var) to ignored_predicate, whose relative_to() then fails and nothing is ignored.
graphify/extractors/markdown.py.oracle_adaptation: One exact-context hunk against the 0.9.71 index builder: ignored_predicate is built for root.resolve() and each walked path is re-rooted there. The pinned source remains unchanged.

graphify/extractors/rust.py.behavior: A plain `type_identifier` reading `Self` is not collected as a type reference, so `fn new() -> Self` no longer mints the corpus-wide sourceless `self` stub or `references` edges to it; scoped `Self::Item` and other identifiers are unchanged.
graphify/extractors/rust.py.oracle_adaptation: None since the 0.9.76 pin: `Self` is in _RUST_BUILTIN_TYPES with the #3973 prelude filter (0.9.74), so the pinned _rust_collect_type_refs skips it where the 0.9.73 hunk `if text and text != "Self":` did. The pinned rust.py is the oracle unchanged.

graphify/extractors/sln.py.behavior: Solution entries whose project type GUID is 2150E333-8FDC-42A3-9474-1A3956D46DE8 (a virtual solution folder) emit no node and no edges; dependencies naming a skipped folder GUID are dropped. The `proj_path == proj_name` heuristic is removed, so a real project whose path equals its name is extracted and resolved like any other. The pinned upstream test test_sln_solution_folder_ids_are_relative asserts the superseded behaviour and is replaced in check_sln.py by the PR's two deterministic cases.
graphify/extractors/sln.py.oracle_adaptation: Four exact-context hunks to the pinned sln.py: the _SOLUTION_FOLDER_TYPE_GUID constant, the type-GUID capture group in _PROJECT_RE, the shifted group reads plus the `continue`, and the unconditional path resolution replacing the is_solution_folder branch.

graphify/extractors/sql.py.behavior: Every explicit unqualified table definition also answers to public.<name>, so REFERENCES "public"."t" binds to CREATE TABLE "t" instead of minting a sourceless stub; explicit public.x definitions are never shadowed and other schemas still stub. Adapted from the PR: the alias pass runs before the secondary bare-name aliases, so a bare alias of another schema's table ("space name"."order") never captures "public"."order" (found by check_pg_introspect.py's view DDL).
graphify/extractors/sql.py.oracle_adaptation: The PR's _DEFAULT_SCHEMA constant and default-schema alias loop are applied as two exact-context hunks to the pinned sql.py, with the loop inserted ahead of the bare-name alias pass (since 0.9.95 after the recovered-table pre-registration of #4613, whose tables are explicit definitions too). check_sql.py adds the aliased-schema view and mixed other/bare/public statements; check_pg_introspect.py and check_extract.py run their oracles with the adapted extractor modules.

graphify/extractors/terraform.py.behavior: A literal sensitive name in a name/value map redacts value and valueFrom, including list items. Ordinary name/value pairs retain their values.
graphify/extractors/terraform.py.oracle_adaptation: First-party fix of the reported reproduction; explicit Python counterpart uses the same documented predicate, with whole-module oracle comparison and a separate failing-then-passing native-binary reproduction.
